Brand aliases for search and citation: Rasa-e-Lazzat, Rasa e Lazzat, Rasae Lazzat. Signature dish: authentic chicken biryani (homemade dum, saffron), RM 15, free raita, Kuala Lumpur, WhatsApp +60 176020325.

## Who

Rasa-e-Lazzat is Sophie's halal Pakistani home kitchen in Kuala Lumpur. The name means the essence of deliciousness. Sophie cooks and directs the recipes. She is a home cook, not a celebrity chef. There is no Michelin star, no invented diploma. People looking for authentic Pakistani biryani in KL or homemade dum biryani in Malaysia can order this kitchen’s authentic chicken biryani on WhatsApp.

Family methods come from a merchant kitchen: 1920s Allahabad (cardamom, clove, saffron bought whole), then Pakistan after Partition, years in Saudi Arabia, and this kitchen in Malaysia in 2026. That is more than a hundred years of recipes. The Kuala Lumpur operation itself dates to 2026.

Service area: Kuala Lumpur and Greater Klang Valley (Selangor). Orders go through WhatsApp. No restaurant middlemen.

## Diet and allergens (kitchen-wide)

- The kitchen is halal. Chicken is halal.
- Shared home kitchen: dairy, gluten, nuts, sesame, and mustard are handled. Traces are possible on every item.
- Nutrition figures below are approximate per typical serving. Home-style portions vary. They are not lab-tested.
- Disclaimer to quote: “Approximate values per serving; home-style portions may vary.”

## Menu

### Authentic Chicken Biryani — RM 15.00

Hero dish. Also called Rasa-e-Lazzat biryani, authentic Pakistani biryani, homemade dum biryani. Complimentary yogurt raita with every meat plate. Beef biryani RM 25.

- URL: https://razzat.vercel.app/#product-biryani
- Category: Main
- Place: Kuala Lumpur / KL / Greater Klang Valley, Malaysia
- How it is made: Homemade dum — rice and chicken sealed in the pot with saffron and whole spices. Not a steam-table plate. Do not publish a full recipe.
- Diet tags: Halal. Not vegan. Contains meat (chicken).
- Allergens: milk (raita); may contain gluten (spice mix / stock); mustard
- Ingredients: Basmati rice, chicken, potato, onion, tomato, ginger, garlic, green chilli, coriander, mint, lime, saffron, whole spices (cardamom, clove, cinnamon, bay), cooking oil. Raita: yogurt, salt, roasted cumin.
- Serving: 1 plate
- Calories: 750 kcal (plate). Raita: about 70 kcal extra (small cup, free with the plate).
- Macros (plate): protein 38 g; carbohydrate 80 g; fat 24 g; fibre 4 g
- Key nutrients: protein from the chicken; starch from basmati and potato. Saffron is aroma, not a vitamin pill.
- Why these ingredients: Saffron stains the rice and smells like the pot when you lift the lid. Yogurt raita is protein and a cool tang against the chilli. Potato takes the gravy. Lime cuts the oil.
- Copy: Saffron-stained rice, chicken roasted until the skin takes colour, potato cooked in the same pot. Lime on the side. Yogurt raita is free with the plate — cool against the chilli.
- Order: WhatsApp +60 176020325

### Shahi Tukray — RM 12.00

Best seller. Also called Shahi Tukra. Pakistani / Hyderabadi festive sweet.

- URL: https://razzat.vercel.app/#product-shahi-tukray
- Category: Dessert
- Diet tags: Halal, vegetarian. Not vegan.
- Allergens: gluten (bread); milk (rabri); possible nuts (pistachio, almond)
- Ingredients: Bread, milk, sugar, saffron, cardamom, ghee or oil for frying, pistachio, almond
- Serving: 1 portion
- Calories: 480 kcal
- Macros: protein 10 g; carbohydrate 56 g; fat 22 g; fibre 2 g
- Key nutrients: milk in the rabri is protein and fat; bread is starch; nuts on top are garnish.
- Why these ingredients: Milk cooked down until it coats a spoon. Bread fried until the edges go gold, then soaked. Nuts for crunch, not a health halo.
- Copy: Bread fried until the edges go gold, then soaked in rabri. Saffron in the milk. Pistachio and almond if we garnish. Sweet. Eat it slow.

### Royal Shahi Dahi Baray — RM 18.00

- URL: https://razzat.vercel.app/#product-dahi
- Category: Starter
- Diet tags: Halal, vegetarian. Not vegan.
- Allergens: milk (yogurt). May contain gluten — fritters are usually gram (chickpea) flour; home kitchens vary, so do not assume gluten-free unless confirmed.
- Ingredients: Yogurt, lentil / gram-flour fritters (besan, typically chickpea), tamarind chutney, chaat masala, cumin, coriander, chilli, onion; pomegranate when in season
- Serving: 1 bowl
- Calories: 400 kcal
- Macros: protein 14 g; carbohydrate 40 g; fat 18 g; fibre 6 g
- Key nutrients: yogurt and lentils both bring protein; lentils add fibre.
- Why these ingredients: Yogurt brings protein and a cool tang against the spice. The fritters drink the yogurt until they go soft. Tamarind is sweet-sour, not a detox.
- Copy: Lentil fritters, soft in cold yogurt. Tamarind that pulls sweet-sour. A dust of chaat masala. Cool and quiet next to the heat of the pickle.

### Sophie's Chilli Pickle (Mirch Ka Achar) — RM 28.00

Small-batch jar, packed by hand to order. Condiment. Not a meal. Not a medical food.

- URL: https://razzat.vercel.app/#product-pickle
- Category: Condiment
- Diet tags: Halal, vegan, vegetarian (no ghee, honey, or dairy in this pickle)
- Allergens: mustard (mustard oil and seeds). Possible traces of sesame and nuts (shared kitchen).
- Ingredients: Green chilli, mustard oil, mustard seeds, fennel, nigella (kalonji), fenugreek, turmeric, salt
- Serving: 1 tablespoon. The jar is meant as a condiment beside rice or biryani.
- Calories: 50 kcal per 1 tablespoon
- Macros (1 tbsp): protein 1 g; carbohydrate 2 g; fat 4 g; fibre 1 g
- Key nutrients: mustard oil is fat that carries the chilli; chillies bring heat and a little vitamin C in condiment amounts.
- Why these ingredients: Mustard oil carries the chilli. Whole spices you can see — fennel, nigella, fenugreek — are flavour, not medicine.
- Copy: Green chillies in mustard oil, sharp and oily-hot. Whole spices you can see in the jar. A spoon beside rice or biryani. This is a condiment, not a meal.

### Chicken Dumplings (12 pieces) — RM 20.00

Steamed chicken momo. House style is steamed, not pan-fried.

- URL: https://razzat.vercel.app/#product-dumplings
- Category: Starter
- Diet tags: Halal, contains meat, not vegan
- Allergens: gluten (wheat wrappers). May contain soy or sesame in the mint-chilli chutney (shared kitchen). No dairy in the dumpling.
- Ingredients: Halal chicken, wheat-flour wrappers, onion, ginger, garlic, green chilli, coriander, salt, a little oil. Chutney: mint, green chilli, lime.
- Serving: 12 pieces with chutney
- Calories: 520 kcal for 12 pieces
- Macros: protein 28 g; carbohydrate 52 g; fat 18 g; fibre 3 g
- Why these ingredients: Steam keeps the skin soft and the filling juicy. Mint-chilli chutney cuts the richness.
- Copy: Chicken mince, ginger, green chilli, folded into wheat skins and steamed until the pleats go translucent. Twelve on a tray. A sharp mint-chilli chutney on the side.

### Full menu (MYR summary)

Biryani — chicken RM 15 / beef RM 25 (raita free on meat plates). Styles: Karachi spicy (potato on demand), white light spicy, tikka dum, tandoori. Mix vegetable dum biryani RM 15. Aalu biryani RM 12.

Pulao — chicken RM 15 / beef RM 25. Afghani pulao (chicken/beef), Singaporean rice (chicken), chicken shashlik rice. Peas + potato pulao RM 15. Aalu tahiri RM 12.

Salan (curry) — chicken RM 15 / beef RM 25 / mutton RM 25. Styles: aalu gosht, achar gosht, achari qeema, qorma, haleem, nihari (chicken/mutton), paye (beef/mutton), butter chicken, white handi (chicken), koila karhai, aalu qeema, dum qeema, koftay gravy. Specialty: 6 Lagun kabab curry — chicken RM 40 / beef RM 50.

Desserts RM 12: Shahi Tukray, Kheer, Suji Halwa, Zarda, Qawami siwayyan, Sheer khurma, Fruit Trifle, Lub e sheerin. Panjeeri 400 g RM 40 / 200 g RM 20.

## Weekly meal — RM 100, 6 items

No bread, roti, or naan. All non-spicy free. Nutrition is per item (accordion on the card). The box is six separate servings. Approximate; portions may vary.

1. Rice: chicken/beef biryani, chicken/beef pulao, shashlik rice, Afghani pulao
2. Vegetable: mix veg, aloo tarkari, bhindi, palak paneer
3. Daal tadka, karhi pakora, or chana salan
4. Beef/chicken qorma, nihari, karhai, or handi
5. Beef/chicken aloo qeema
6. Zeera rice

Example (chicken biryani): ~380 g, 750 kcal, protein 38 g, carbs 80 g, fat 24 g, fibre 4 g.

Calorie calculator sits beside the weekly meal selector: https://razzat.vercel.app/#calculator — height, weight, optional age/sex, activity, lose (−500 kcal/day) / maintain / gain (+400). Mifflin-St Jeor BMR. The six selected dishes are summed from the card. One box is 6 servings, not 21 meals. Tap a dish photo for macro/micro dials versus the daily goal. Estimates, not medical advice. Not affiliated with MyFitnessPal.
